primitives.name: Pre-Snap Position Clustering
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Clustering: positions of each WR/TE/RB/FB (and CB/FS/SS/ILB) stored **relative to the ball**, then **k-means per player** on the snap x/y, cluster number + x/y fed to a neural network.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'x, y': 'meters relative to ball center', 'cluster_number': 'dimensionless integer [1, K]', 'K': 'number of clusters'}
primitives.assumptions: Player positions are stationary pre-snap; spatial proximity implies tactical relevance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When players exceed 10-yard radius from ball, clustering becomes unreliable.

layer2.mapping: Each player's cluster index encodes positional leverage; neural network learns mapping to coverage type.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of predicted coverage shell against actual post-snap result.

primitives.name: Spatial Leverage Encoding
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Method, verbatim - Pre-snap inputs: down, distance, field position, **hash (five buckets: L, L-Mid, Mid, R-Mid, R)**, offensive personnel (RB/FB count, TE count), score differential, and **per-player pre-snap position clusters**.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'hash_bucket': 'categorical {L, L-Mid, Mid, R-Mid, R}', 'offensive_personnel': 'count vector [RB, FB, TE]', 'score_differential': 'points'}
primitives.assumptions: Hash bucketing captures alignment bias; personnel counts reflect formation intent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Inconsistent hash labeling or missing personnel data leads to misclassification.

layer2.mapping: Combines hash, personnel, and cluster data into a feature kernel for predictive modeling.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between encoded features and observed defensive adjustments.

primitives.name: Coverage Shell Prediction
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Post-snap outputs predicted: run/pass, man/zone, coverage shell (Cover 1, Cover 3, ...).
primitives.assumptions: Coverage decisions are deterministic functions of pre-snap configuration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High variance in post-snap execution undermines prediction reliability.

layer2.mapping: Neural network maps cluster + context features to discrete coverage shell class.
layer2.telemetry: F1-score of predicted coverage shell vs. ground truth.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism involves transforming absolute player coordinates into relative ball-space clusters using k-means. Each player’s cluster index encodes their spatial relationship to the ball, enabling a compact representation of leverage. These clusters, combined with contextual variables like hash and personnel, form a feature vector input to a neural network. The network learns to map this vector to post-snap outcomes such as run/pass and coverage type. Dualities emerge in that the same spatial configuration can imply different strategic interpretations depending on game state. Failure modes include misclustered players due to noise or outliers, and overfitting when too many features are used without regularization. The method assumes static pre-snap alignment, which may not hold under dynamic motion.
